sense: a person of learning and ideas

terms.grammar: noun with the adjective doctus, docta, doctum
evidence: Cic. Brut. 114: doctus vir et Graecīs litterīs ērudītus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Doctus, the participle of doceō: taught, and so learned, skilled (Lewis & Short). In the plural, doctī, the learned.
Literally “brought out of roughness”, from ērudiō: trained, accomplished.
Learned in books and literature; literally marked with letters, and so in Plautus a branded slave (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: doctus vir et Graecīs litterīs ērudītus
phrases.english: a learned man, trained in Greek letters

phrases.latin: Canius nec īnfacētus et satis litterātus
phrases.english: Canius, a man not without wit and well enough read

sources: Lewis & Short: doceo · Lewis & Short: eruditus · Lewis & Short: litteratus
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
